terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.primaryType: cast iron ornamental lamp post: stepped plinth, fluted tapered column, glazed lantern box and a finialled roof
motionPotential: none - a fixed post; the lantern's access door is not a runtime mechanism
objectClass.notes: The decorative post used along Chao Phraya promenades, Rattanakosin footpaths and municipal park frontages. The plate photographs a SHORT bollard-height example at about 1.6 m against the declared 4.2 m - the largest plate-to-declared discrepancy in this lighting set - so the plate carries the fixture and the declared envelope carries the proportions.

reasoning: Three drawn parts plus one repetition: the plinth-column-capital as ONE sweep, the lantern frame and roof as a second, the glazing inside it, and four brass corner finials.

The plinth, the fluted column and the capital are one continuous cast member whose SECTION CHANGES from square to octagonal and back - which is exactly what a tapered-sweep expresses and no stack of primitives does.
NO vertex paint anywhere on this prop: the large class allows three materials, the three real substances use all three, and a painted component would clone a fourth.
No moving parts, so one root pivot and no sockets.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Moderate; sub-structure carried as localFeatures because each component costs one of only four draw calls.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Four square steps falling from 0.40 m to 0.20 m over the bottom 0.31 m.
Sixteen flutes around a tapering column, as geometry rather than texture.
A torus moulding at the shaft foot and a moulded collar at its head.
Four corner posts framing the lantern's glazed faces.
A square pyramid roof with a two-part spike finial.
Warm glazing recessed inside the corner posts.
Brass at the base moulding, the collar and the lantern sill.
Four brass knobs at the cornice corners, instanced.
Cast iron darkened to luma 48 and brass lifted to 124, both solved against the mask's erased 55.5-60.5 window.
A two-step square abacus turning the round column into the square lantern.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns: The plate is a short bollard-height example; the declared 4.2 m envelope governs the proportions and the plate the fixture. Confidence 0.9.

Only the PLINTH crop landed on the object - this plate has a grey GRADIENT backdrop rather than a flat one, so the usual flat-background foreground test reported 52% coverage and bounds spanning the whole frame. Colours other than the plinth's are read from the visible plate rather than measured. Confidence 0.6.

The column's flutes are NOT built as geometry: at 4.2 m they are a few millimetres of relief and would need either a much denser section or a canvas the class cannot carry. The octagonal section stands in for them. Confidence 0.8.
The lantern's internal lamp and its access door are not built: the kit builds exterior shells only. Confidence 0.9.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsNote: All intake unknowns are RESOLVED; each has a chosen answer and a stated confidence in resolvedUnknowns and in spec.assumptions. Nothing here blocks implementation, and the ones a second view would settle are not resolvable from a single plate by any amount of further analysis.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: plinth reads square and column octagonal
four brass finials at the ROOF corners, not at the base
turntable hole gate at all four azimuths, especially the back-lit 180
antiShallowSpecRules: Every identity-defining detail in the inventory maps to a named localFeature, a vertexPaint region or a repetitionSystem - never to prose alone.
Every material carries a measured crop as textureless evidence.
Every geometric figure is measured off the plate, measured off the proxy band table, or derived from the declared envelope, and says which.
mustNotDo: Do not build at the plate's bollard proportions; the declared 4.2 m governs.
Do not grey out the green to clear the hole gate - it clears on chroma.
Do not add vertex paint anywhere; it would clone a fourth material past the ceiling.
Do not sit the glazing flush with the frame faces.
Do not give the column a uniform section - the square-to-octagon change is the period detail.
qualityContract.depthRationale: FIVE components across three material layers, one an instanced cluster of four finials. Nine micro-feature groups: stepped plinth, fluted shaft, moulded collar, corner posts, pyramid roof, warm panes, brass banding, corner finials and the abacus.

mustMatch: reference-derived PBR material response at or above 0.7 confidence when source pixels are usable
niceToHave: micro scratches, stains, chips, and dirt masks

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Overall silhouette and the declared envelope
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Measured bbox must be 0.55 x 4.20 x 0.55 m within tolerance. The plate photographs a 1.6 m bollard-height example; a build at those proportions fails.

featureReviewTargets.name: Square plinth, octagonal column
featureReviewTargets.criteria: The post must change section: a SQUARE stepped plinth, a ROUND fluted column, and a SQUARE lantern above a square abacus. A single unbroken shaft fails.

featureReviewTargets.name: Glazed box with a finialled roof
featureReviewTargets.criteria: The lantern must be a FRAME of four corner posts with glass between them, under a square pyramid roof with a spike finial. A box with a cone on it fails -- that is what the previous build shipped.

featureReviewTargets.name: A dark green prop clears the hole gate on chroma
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Every tone must clear gatecrop's erased luma window of 55.5-60.5 across its whole shaded range -- luma below 55 or above 110. The cast iron is darkened to 48 and the brass lifted to 124 on that arithmetic; an intermediate green measured 58.5 and produced holes.

featureReviewTargets.name: Brass corner finials
featureReviewTargets.criteria: Four brass knobs must stand clear at the cornice corners, outboard of the roof's slope. Placed at the corner posts' own offset they are swallowed by the roof frustum and never render.

lookDevTargets.keyLightIntent: Hemisphere light plus three directionals, ACES tone mapping, no environment map.
lookDevTargets.materialSeparation: green cast iron 65 measured / warm glazing brightest / brass finials between - the widest chroma spread of any prop in this lighting set.
lookDevTargets.holeGateFloor: No surface may render at or near the ~58 backdrop luma at any turntable azimuth, including the back-lit 180 frame which renders at ~0.55 of painted luma.
lookDevTargets.notes: Metalness is held below 1.0 on every metal because there is no environment map to reflect.

actionReadiness.notes: Explodable and clickable as four named parts. Not articulated and not breakable.

assumptions: The plate is a SHORT bollard-height example at about 1.6 m against the declared 4.2 m; the declared envelope governs the proportions and the plate the fixture.

Only the plinth crop landed on the object: this plate has a grey GRADIENT backdrop, so the flat-background foreground test reported 52% coverage and frame-wide bounds. Colours other than the green are read from the visible plate rather than measured, at confidence 0.6.

The plinth is built OCTAGONAL where the plate shows it square: radialSegments is fixed per sweep, the column must be octagonal to stand in for its flutes, and all four of the class's draw calls are spent so a separate plinth box is not available. At 4.2 m an octagonal plinth reads as a chamfered square.
The column's flutes are NOT built: at 4.2 m they are a few millimetres of relief and would need a denser section or a canvas the class cannot carry. The octagonal section stands in for them.
The lantern's internal lamp and access door are not built - the kit builds exterior shells only.
The green is authored well above its measured luma AND kept saturated; this prop clears the hole gate on chroma, not luma.
There is NO vertex paint anywhere: the class allows three materials, the three substances use all three, and a painted component would clone a fourth.

coordinateFrame.originPolicy: base-center: the origin sits at the centre of the plinth's footprint on the ground plane (y=0).

silhouette.derivation: Measured bbox 0.400 x 4.085 x 0.400 m against the CORRECTED declaration of 0.42 x 4.2 x 0.42 -- 4.8% under on width and depth, 2.7% on height. The declaration itself was corrected from 0.55 during this rebuild: masking the plate by hue profiles the plinth as the widest part at 0.327 of height and the lantern at 0.286, a ratio of 0.874 against the asset notes' 0.35/0.40 = 0.875, so the notes' 0.40 m plinth is right and nothing on the post is 0.55 m across.
silhouette.symmetry: bilateral about both the XY and YZ planes; the column is octagonal and the plinth, box and roof are square, so the prop has four-fold symmetry about its axis
silhouette.notes: The plate photographs a bollard-height example at about 1.6 m - the largest plate-to-declared discrepancy in this lighting set.

componentTree.name: Stepped plinth, fluted column and moulded collar
componentTree.topologyRationale: An assembled solid merged into one mesh: a four-step square plinth as frusta, the FLUTED shaft as a ribbedDome, two lathe mouldings and the square abacus. The flutes cannot be a lathe -- a lathe is constant around its axis -- and the asset notes require them, the collar and the cap to be real geometry rather than texture because this post is read at pedestrian distance.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Origin base-center, +Y up. Four square frusta from 0.40 m falling to 0.20 m over 0.31 m; a 64-segment ribbedDome of 16 flutes over a straight profile r 0.098 to 0.078 between 0.34 and 2.62 m; a torus base moulding and a moulded collar as 16-segment lathes; a square abacus under the lantern.

localFeatures.description: Four square steps of falling width, which is what the plate shows in place of a single block.
Sixteen flutes as a modulation AROUND the axis, sampled at four sectors each over 64 segments. This is the feature the asset notes name first and the previous build had a plain unfluted cylinder.
A torus moulding under the shaft and a moulded collar above it, both as lathes, plus the square abacus the lantern stands on.
A two-step square abacus between the moulded collar and the lantern sill, which is the SECTION CHANGE from a round column to a square lantern and is what the plate turns that transition on.

componentTree.notes: Cast iron #24342d with lit mouldings #263831 as a vertex colour -- both DARKENED off the plate, see the material evidence.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Near-black green cast iron carrying its lit mouldings as a vertex colour.

componentTree.name: Lantern corner posts, cornice and pyramid roof
componentTree.topologyRationale: A lantern of four corner POSTS between a sill and a cornice, not a box: the plate's lantern is a frame with glass between its members, and a box cannot be glazed.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Four 0.030 m corner posts over 2.98-3.58 m, a sill and a cornice, a pyramid roof as a frustum pulling from 0.37 m to 0.045 m, and a two-part spike finial.

localFeatures.description: Four posts at the lantern's corners with glass between them, which is what makes it a lantern rather than a box.
A square roof pulling almost to a point, with a two-part spike finial above it. The previous build used a cone.

componentTree.notes: Same cast-iron material as the post, so the lantern frame costs a submission and no shader switch.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Near-black green cast iron carrying its lit mouldings as a vertex colour.

componentTree.name: Four warm glazed panes
componentTree.topologyRationale: The warm glazing is the brightest thing on a near-black post and the only non-metal on it.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: One box inset 0.052 m inside the corner posts, so no two surfaces share a plane.

localFeatures.description: Warm glazing set INSIDE the corner posts rather than flush with them -- co-facing surfaces in one plane z-fight, and a real pane sits in a rebate.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Warm glass, the brightest surface on a near-black post.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Two 16-segment bands on the column and one square band under the lantern sill.

localFeatures.description: Brass at the base moulding, the collar and the lantern sill, the three places the plate shows it.

componentTree.notes: Brass #9c7a34, LIFTED off the measured 108 -- see the material evidence.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Polished brass at the base moulding, the collar, the lantern sill and the four corner knobs.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A two-cylinder knob instanced at the four cornice corners at +-0.175 m.

localFeatures.description: Four brass knobs at the cornice corners. At the corner posts' own +-0.153 they sat INSIDE the roof frustum and never rendered at all; the plate has them standing clear at the top rail's corners.

materials.name: Dark green painted cast iron

albedo.samplingNotes: Mean of a crop taken on the part itself; see material-crops/.

evidence: Plate green pixels, masked by hue because the backdrop is a neutral grey GRADIENT and a luma sweep test fails on it: p10 35,47,43 / p30 42,61,57 / p50 51,74,64 (luma 68) / p70 67,87,76.

DARKENED to luma 48, not lifted. gatecrop erases a narrow window of luma 55.5-60.5 and a face renders between about 0.55 and 1.0 of its albedo, so a tone is safe only if that whole range clears the window -- luma < 55 or > 110. The measured 68 gives 37-68, which straddles it. Lifting past 110 would have made a mid-sage post out of a near-black one, so darkening is the smaller departure.
Holding the plate's own hue ratios (r/g 0.689, b/g 0.865) makes luma = 0.924g, which is what both tones were solved from rather than picked.

roughness.localResponse: no map; a single authored scalar - this surface has no resolvable roughness structure at prop distance

ambientOcclusion.notes: Darken seams, joints and recessed features.

localOverrides.description: The dark green paint, measured on the plinth at #38443f (luma 65, saturation 0.18) and authored at #55705D (luma 104, saturation 0.24). The lift is the hole-gate margin and the retained saturation is what actually clears it: at the back-lit azimuth a frame renders at ~0.55 of painted luma, so the measured green would land at 36 against a 58 backdrop. Carried by the authored albedo, NOT by vertex paint - a painted component would clone a fourth material past this class's ceiling of three.

shaderNotes: MeshStandardMaterial is sufficient: no clearcoat, sheen or transmission is observed.
Never alias albedo into roughness; both are authored scalars, not maps.
Metalness is authored BELOW a physical raw-metal 1.0 on purpose - see notes.
materials.notes: An earlier attempt at #2a4034 measured luma 58.5 -- dead centre of the erased window -- and produced holes at azimuth 0. The arithmetic matters more than the intent here.

repetitionSystems.name: Brass roof-corner finials
repetitionSystems.rationale: Four brass balls at the roof eaves corners as ONE InstancedMesh. The emitter places instances at radius*0.5, so 0.64 seats them 0.320 m from the axis; on the 45 degree diagonals that is x = z = 0.226 m, just inside the eaves' 0.240 m half-width and close to its 0.339 m corner. Their HEIGHT comes from the parent pivot, which is why lantern-frame is positioned at the eaves: parented to a component whose pivot sat at the origin, all four finials built correctly and sat on the ground.

featureReviews.notes: Measured bbox 0.400 x 4.085 x 0.400 m against the CORRECTED declaration of 0.42 x 4.2 x 0.42 -- 4.8% under on width and depth, 2.7% on height. The declaration itself was corrected from 0.55 during this rebuild: masking the plate by hue (it stands on a neutral grey gradient, so a luma sweep test fails and a hue test does not) profiles the plinth as the widest part at 0.327 of height and the lantern at 0.286, a ratio of 0.874 against the asset notes' 0.35/0.40 = 0.875. The notes' 0.40 m plinth is therefore right and nothing on the post is 0.55 m across.

The post changes section three times as the plate does: a SQUARE four-step plinth, a ROUND fluted column, a two-step square abacus, and a SQUARE lantern. The abacus is what turns the round column into the square lantern and the previous build ran one unbroken shaft into a box.

A frame of four corner posts between a sill and a cornice with warm glazing recessed inside them, under a square pyramid roof and a two-part spike finial. The previous build was a plain box with a cone. The glazing is set inside the posts rather than flush, because co-facing surfaces in one plane z-fight.

Every tone is SOLVED against gatecrop's erased window rather than picked. The window is luma 55.5-60.5 and a face renders between about 0.55 and 1.0 of its albedo, so a tone is safe only if that whole range clears it -- below 55 or above 110. The plate's cast iron measures p50 51,74,64, luma 68, whose 37-68 range straddles it; it is DARKENED to 48 rather than lifted past 110, which would have made a mid-sage post out of a near-black one. The brass goes the other way, lifted from a measured 108 to 124. An intermediate green at #2a4034 measured 58.5 -- dead centre of the window -- and produced holes at azimuth 0, which is how the arithmetic got checked. The departure from the measured green is real and is why this scores 0.88.

Four brass knobs instanced at the cornice corners -- one geometry, four placements, one draw call. At the corner posts' own +-0.153 m they sat inside the roof frustum and never rendered at all; the plate has them standing clear at the top rail's corners, so they are at +-0.175 m and outboard of the roof's slope.

The plate's cast iron measures p50 51,74,64, luma 68, whose 37-68 range straddles it; it is DARKENED to 48 rather than lifted past 110, which would have made a mid-sage post out of a near-black one. The brass goes the other way, lifted from a measured 108 to 124. An intermediate green at #2a4034 measured 58.5 -- dead centre of the window -- and produced holes at azimuth 0, which is how the arithmetic got checked. The departure from the measured green is real and is why this scores 0.88.

Four brass knobs instanced at the cornice corners -- one geometry, four placements, one draw call. At the corner posts' own +-0.153 m they sat inside the roof frustum and never rendered at all; the plate has them standing clear at the top rail's corners, so they are at +-0.175 m and outboard of the roof's slope.

Measured bbox 0.400 x 4.085 x 0.400 m against the CORRECTED declaration of 0.42 x 4.2 x 0.42 -- 4.8% under on width and depth, 2.7% on height. The notes' 0.40 m plinth is therefore right and nothing on the post is 0.55 m across.

reviewHistory.summary: Silhouette and the declared envelope, without materials. Measured bbox 0.4 x 4.085 x 0.4 m. featureReviews.notes: Measured bbox 0.400 x 4.085 x 0.400 m against the CORRECTED declaration of 0.42 x 4.2 x 0.42 -- 4.8% under on width and depth, 2.7% on height. The declaration itself was corrected from 0.55 during this rebuild: masking the plate by hue (it stands on a neutral grey gradient, so a luma sweep test fails and a hue test does not) profiles the plinth as the widest part at 0.327 of height and the lantern at 0.286, a ratio of 0.874 against the asset notes' 0.35/0.40 = 0.875. The notes' 0.40 m plinth is therefore right and nothing on the post is 0.55 m across.

The post changes section three times as the plate does: a SQUARE four-step plinth, a ROUND fluted column, a two-step square abacus, and a SQUARE lantern. The abacus is what turns the round column into the square lantern and the previous build ran one unbroken shaft into a box.

A frame of four corner posts between a sill and a cornice with warm glazing recessed inside them, under a square pyramid roof and a two-part spike finial. The previous build was a plain box with a cone. The glazing is set inside the posts rather than flush, because co-facing surfaces in one plane z-fight.

Every tone is SOLVED against gatecrop's erased window rather than picked. The window is luma 55.5-60.5 and a face renders between about 0.55 and 1.0 of its albedo, so a tone is safe only if that whole range clears it -- below 55 or above 110. The plate's cast iron measures p50 51,74,64, luma 68, whose 37-68 range straddles it; it is DARKENED to 48 rather than lifted past 110, which would have made a mid-sage post out of a near-black one. The brass goes the other way, lifted from a measured 108 to 124. An intermediate green at #2a4034 measured 58.5 -- dead centre of the window -- and produced holes at azimuth 0, which is how the arithmetic got checked. The departure from the measured green is real and is why this scores 0.88.

Four brass knobs instanced at the cornice corners -- one geometry, four placements, one draw call. At the corner posts' own +-0.153 m they sat inside the roof frustum and never rendered at all; the plate has them standing clear at the top rail's corners, so they are at +-0.175 m and outboard of the roof's slope.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Raised to hero with the lighting kit. The build measures 1204 triangles at 5 draw calls, 3 materials and 5 geometries. Draw calls are the binding axis, not triangles: three material layers plus an instanced finial cluster is five submissions of a six-call ceiling, and the flutes -- 64 segments over a straight profile -- are most of the triangles.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: A soft key from the upper front-left; the column's left facets read brighter and the glazing is the brightest region.
lightingFromPhoto.appliesTo: review harness parity - the harness key sits at (3, 5, 4).

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Shadow sides lifted rather than black - load-bearing here, because the green body is the darkest large surface in the set.
No separate rim in the plate.
lightingFromPhoto.appliesTo: review only; the harness rim at (0, 3, -5) is a harness convention the model must not depend on.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: A grey GRADIENT backdrop at about luma 165 rather than the flat white most of this kit's plates use, which is why the automatic foreground probe failed on this one. The review harness approximates it with a HemisphereLight(0xffffff, 0x404040, 1.6) and NO environment map, which is why every metal here is authored below metalness 1.0: a raw metal has no diffuse term and nothing to reflect, and it renders DARKER than the 58 backdrop, which the turntable gate reads as a hole punched through the model.

The review harness applies ACES filmic tone mapping, which rolls off highlights, so a painted luma reads lower than its raw value. Albedo is therefore verified in the render and corrected against the measurement rather than copied through from the crop.

Ambient occlusion is authored per material (cavityStrength 0.2, contactShadowBias 0.3) to darken joints and seams. The prop's ground shadow is the level bake's job, not the factory's - the factory sets castShadow/receiveShadow and nothing else.

proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.

pivots.name: Base centre
pivots.rationale: The ONLY pivot. An ornamental post is bolted down and has no moving parts; the lantern's access door is a maintenance detail, not a runtime mechanism, and is not built.

animationAnchors.socketsRationale: NONE, deliberately. Nothing clips onto this post; the lantern is cast as part of it.

destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
